## Purpose and Scopesvg image

This document describes the internal architecture of the Contexter system, including its layered design, module organization, and how CLI commands map to implementation modules. It explains the structural decisions that enable dual-format support, shared utilities, and extensibility.

For detailed documentation of the shared utility functions, see [Utility Layer (contexter\_utils)](/ray0404/Contexter/6.3-utility-layer-(contexter_utils)). For specific implementation details about context file formats and parsing logic, see [Technical Details](/ray0404/Contexter/7-technical-details). For information about external library usage, see [Dependencies](/ray0404/Contexter/6.4-dependencies).

## High-Level System Designsvg image

The Contexter system implements a three-layer architecture: a CLI interface layer, an implementation module layer, and a shared utility layer. This design provides clear separation between user interaction, business logic, and common functionality.

### Layered Architecturesvg image

**Diagram: Three-Layer System Architecture**

The architecture enforces strict layering:

- **CLI Interface Layer**: Thin command-line entry points that parse arguments and invoke module functions
- **Implementation Module Layer**: Contains business logic for each operation
- **Shared Utility Layer**: Provides common functionality used across all modules
- **External Dependencies**: Third-party libraries accessed through the utility layer

This design enables:

- Independent testing of module logic without CLI parsing overhead
- Programmatic use of modules from other Python code
- Centralized dependency management through `contexter_utils`
- Clear maintenance boundaries between interface and implementation

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L36) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29)

### Command-to-Module Mappingsvg image

Each CLI command maps to exactly one implementation module through entry points defined in `setup.py`. This 1:1 relationship ensures consistent behavior and simplifies the system's mental model.

**Diagram: Entry Point to Module Mapping**

| CLI Command | Entry Point Target | Module File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `buildcontext` | `context_builder:main` | `context_builder.py` |
| `reconstructor` | `reconstructor:main` | `reconstructor.py` |
| `updatecontext` | `update_context:main` | `update_context.py` |
| `updater` | `updater:main` | `updater.py` |
| `smartupdate` | `smart_update:main` | `smart_update.py` |
| `sanitizecontext` | `sanitize_context:main` | `sanitize_context.py` |
| `md2html` | `md2html:main` | `md2html.py` |
| `html2md` | `html2md:main` | `html2md.py` |
| `buildcontexthtml` | `build_context_html:main` | `build_context_html.py` |
| `reconstructorhtml` | `reconstructor_html:main` | `reconstructor_html.py` |
| `updatecontexthtml` | `update_context_html:main` | `update_context_html.py` |
| `updaterhtml` | `updater_html:main` | `updater_html.py` |

Each module exposes a `main()` function that serves as the entry point when invoked from the command line. This standard interface makes the system easy to extend—adding a new command requires creating a module with a `main()` function and registering it in `setup.py`.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53)

## Format Duality Architecturesvg image

The system implements parallel processing pipelines for Markdown and HTML formats. This dual-format design allows users to work in their preferred format while maintaining feature parity across most operations.

**Diagram: Parallel Format Pipelines**

### Pipeline Asymmetriessvg image

While both pipelines support core operations, there are notable differences:

| Feature | Markdown Pipeline | HTML Pipeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | `context_builder.py` | `build_context_html.py` |
| Reconstruct | `reconstructor.py` | `reconstructor_html.py` |
| Standard Update | `update_context.py` | `update_context_html.py` |
| Apply Update | `updater.py` | `updater_html.py` |
| Smart Update | `smart_update.py` | ❌ Not available |
| AI Sanitization | `sanitize_context.py` | ❌ Not available |

The Markdown pipeline includes `smart_update.py` for rsync-based high-performance updates and `sanitize_context.py` for AI workflow integration. These features are not present in the HTML pipeline, suggesting that Markdown is the primary working format while HTML serves as an output/distribution format.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L36) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md20-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L20-L36)

## Module Organizationsvg image

The twelve implementation modules are organized into four functional groups:

**Diagram: Functional Module Groups**

### Module Groupssvg image

**Building Modules** (2 modules)

- `context_builder.py`: Scans directories and generates Markdown context files
- `build_context_html.py`: Scans directories and generates HTML context files

**Reconstruction Modules** (2 modules)

- `reconstructor.py`: Parses Markdown context files and recreates directory structures
- `reconstructor_html.py`: Parses HTML context files and recreates directory structures

**Update Modules** (5 modules)

- `update_context.py`: Generates diff-based patches between Markdown contexts
- `updater.py`: Applies patches to Markdown context files
- `smart_update.py`: Generates rsync-based patches with higher efficiency
- `update_context_html.py`: Generates patches between HTML contexts
- `updater_html.py`: Applies patches to HTML context files

**Utility Modules** (3 modules)

- `sanitize_context.py`: Fixes formatting issues in AI-generated Markdown
- `md2html.py`: Converts Markdown context files to HTML format
- `html2md.py`: Converts HTML context files to Markdown format

All twelve modules depend on `contexter_utils.py` for shared functionality including file I/O, parsing, formatting, and external library access. This centralization prevents code duplication and ensures consistent behavior across all commands.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L36) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md20-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L20-L36)

## Entry Point Configurationsvg image

CLI commands are registered in `setup.py` through the setuptools entry points mechanism. This configuration makes the commands globally accessible after installation.

### Entry Points Declarationsvg image

The `setup.py` file declares all entry points in the `entry_points` dictionary:

Each entry follows the pattern: `command_name=module_name:function_name`

When a user runs a command like `buildcontext`, Python's entry point system:

1. Locates the `context_builder` module
2. Calls the `main()` function within that module
3. Passes command-line arguments to the function

This mechanism provides:

- **Platform independence**: Works across Windows, Linux, and macOS
- **Virtual environment isolation**: Commands are scoped to the environment
- **Clean uninstallation**: Commands are removed when the package is uninstalled
- **Standard interface**: All commands follow the same invocation pattern

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53)

### Module Registrationsvg image

The `setup.py` file also declares all modules in the `py_modules` list:

This list tells setuptools which Python files to include in the package. Each module in this list corresponds to a `.py` file in the project root directory.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L36)

## Dependency Managementsvg image

External dependencies are specified in two locations:

| File | Purpose | Dependencies Listed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pyproject.toml` | PEP 517/518 build metadata | `markdown`, `Pygments`, `markdownify`, `beautifulsoup4`, `patch` |
| `requirements.txt` | Traditional pip requirements | Same dependencies (read by `setup.py`) |

The `setup.py` file reads `requirements.txt` at build time to populate the `install_requires` list:

This approach maintains compatibility with both modern PEP 517 builds and traditional setuptools workflows.

**Dependency Purposes:**

- **`markdown`**: Converts Markdown to HTML for HTML context file generation
- **`Pygments`**: Provides syntax highlighting for code blocks in context files
- **`beautifulsoup4`**: Parses HTML context files during reconstruction
- **`markdownify`**: Converts HTML back to Markdown for format conversion
- **`patch`**: Implements diff/patch operations for update functionality

All modules access these dependencies through imports in `contexter_utils.py`, establishing a single point of dependency management.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py10-12](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L10-L12) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py38](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L38-L38)

## Design Rationalesvg image

The architectural decisions in Contexter support specific goals:

**1:1 Command-Module Mapping**: Simplifies the system's mental model. Users can expect one module per command, making the codebase predictable and easy to navigate.

**Shared Utility Layer**: Prevents code duplication across twelve modules. Common operations like file reading, binary detection, and language inference are implemented once in `contexter_utils.py`.

**Thin CLI Layer**: Entry points are minimal wrappers that parse arguments and call module functions. This allows modules to be imported and used programmatically without CLI overhead.

**Dual-Format Support**: Enables users to choose their preferred format based on workflow requirements—Markdown for text-based editing and AI integration, HTML for web-based viewing and distribution.

**Centralized Dependencies**: All external libraries are imported through `contexter_utils.py`. This makes dependency management straightforward and enables easy mocking for testing.

**Modular Extension**: Adding new functionality requires creating a new module file and registering it in `setup.py`. No changes to existing modules are necessary.

This architecture balances simplicity with extensibility, making Contexter easy to understand, maintain, and extend.
